Energy built steadily from a scattered opening into a booked appointment with a specific day and time, though the underlying property (commercial-adjacent nonprofit, possible ground mount, comparison-shopping across multiple companies) creates real fragility the rep never explicitly flagged as unusual.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag unknown, but observed transcript supports 'booked' — a specific day (Tuesday the 3rd) and time (9AM) were mutually agreed at 06:50-06:58. However this booking sits on an unresolved scope question: the property is a nonprofit/LLC-owned educational facility with sponsorship/promotional questions raised at 00:12 and 01:12-01:20 that the rep never addressed, and it's unclear whether Ion's standard residential program even fits this use case.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. Exactly. So we'll need to we don't do the groundnuts here at ION, so we'll primarily focus on that Northern building.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer described a mixed-use, multi-structure nonprofit property considering a ground-mount layout — a scenario outside Ion's standard single-family residential script. The rep handles it inline by stating a company fact (no ground mounts) and redirecting to the roof, without pausing to flag internally that this property type itself may need special handling before booking. This is a plausible, well-supported reactive read, but the alternative — that stating a known company capability limit accurately IS the correct move and needs no escalation — is at least equally supported, since the rep had the fact readily available and used it correctly.
